answer: Cross-epoch consistency scoring: each identity must reproduce its prior behavioural profile across epochs, scored against a stored relic of its last signed interaction trace. A sybil cluster that reuses one trace template shows correlated drift and gets its cross-epoch score dropped below threshold, so the orchard of distinct histories cannot be faked cheaply. The attacker then pays one full organic interaction history per identity, since shared or copied traces fail the drift check each epoch. Sustaining that history across an ocean of epochs multiplies the cost linearly per identity.
